text:
maya: Heads-up — bringing up a new embed candidate 'cerulean-v1' for onboarding. Ran a quick int8 pass on the small holdout and seeing a recall@10 dip when batch sizes increase. Can we run a focused batch-size sensitivity sweep + clustering stability? Need recall@1/5/10, silhouette, and per-lang centroid drift.

liam: On it. I'll run a sweep on staging 10k holdout. What are our baselines to compare? :mag:

maya: Baseline is heron-embed-compact (int8): recall@10 = 0.87, recall@1 = 0.67, silhouette ~0.44. Target is >= baseline or explainable trade-off with cost.

sophie: I'll add UMAP + HDBSCAN stability checks and JS divergence on centroids across languages.

ashok: FYI runtime note — our serving runtime does kernel selection switching around certain batch shapes. That can change FP fallback behavior and numerical kernels, which could affect quality. Worth checking kernel logs.

liam: Running command now:
```
./eval/run_embed_onboard.sh \
  --model cerulean-v1 \
  --quant int8 \
  --batch-sizes 1,8,16,32,64,128 \
  --holdout /datasets/emb_holdout_10k.jsonl \
  --metrics recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,silhouette \
  --per-lang en,fr,ja \
```

eval-bot: Sweep finished (quick summary) — raw logs in /tmp/cerulean_batch_sweep.log. Summary: 
batch=1   recall@1=0.672 recall@5=0.802 recall@10=0.884 silhouette=0.442
batch=8   recall@1=0.668 recall@5=0.797 recall@10=0.878 silhouette=0.440
batch=16  recall@1=0.660 recall@5=0.789 recall@10=0.869 silhouette=0.436
batch=32  recall@1=0.645 recall@5=0.770 recall@10=0.852 silhouette=0.423
batch=64  recall@1=0.612 recall@5=0.731 recall@10=0.832 silhouette=0.401
batch=128 recall@1=0.585 recall@5=0.700 recall@10=0.801 silhouette=0.378

eval-bot: Per-lang delta (recall@10 vs batch=1): en=-0.018, fr=-0.035, ja=-0.083.

liam: Whoa — sharp drop for ja at 64+. Looks like sequence length distribution is heavier for ja (lots of long queries). Could be KV cache eviction / attention kernel fallback.

ashok: I pulled the runtime inspect for the same run:
```
$ grpcurl -plaintext -d '{"model":"cerulean-v1","op":"kernels"}' localhost:8080/inspect
{
  "batch_shapes": ["1x512","8x512","16x512","32x512","64x512","128x512"],
  "selected_kernels": ["fast_fused_attn","fast_fused_attn","fast_fused_attn","fallback_fp16_kernels","fallback_fp16_kernels","fallback_fp16_kernels"]
}
```
So kernel selection flips at 32->64 which matches the quality drop.

sophie: Kernel flip explains numerical differences. Also saw HDBSCAN cluster purity drop: N_clusters stable until 32, then fragmentation at 64+. UMAP embedding spread increases (centroid drift).

maya: OK. Two hypotheses: (1) kernel fallback at large batch sizes introduces small numeric differences that hurt nearest-neighbour ranking for long queries, (2) per-channel quantization vs per-tensor might interact. Let's do controlled runs:
- run batch 64 with env var FORCE_KERNEL=fast_fused_attn to force fused kernel (if available)
- rerun quantization using per-channel qparams (if not done)
- rerun with disable_prefix_cache=true to avoid cache interference

liam: I'll kick those off. Command I'm using for the forced kernel test: 
```
FORCE_KERNEL=fast_fused_attn ./eval/run_embed_onboard.sh --model cerulean-v1 --quant int8 --batch-sizes 64 --holdout /datasets/emb_holdout_10k.jsonl --metrics recall@1,recall@10
```

infra-bot: Deploy note — forcing kernels may hit unsupported ops on some GPU instances; put a small canary tag.

eval-bot: Forced-kernel run results: batch=64 (FORCE_KERNEL=fused) recall@10=0.848 recall@1=0.631 silhouette=0.414. Improvement vs fallback but still below batch=1.

sophie: Per-channel quantization run (int8-perchannel) results: batch=64 recall@10=0.856 recall@1=0.645 silhouette=0.428. Much closer to baseline.

liam: disable_prefix_cache run shows minor improvement (recall@10=0.840). So biggest wins are per-channel quant and forcing fused kernel when available.

maya: Great — actionable summary:
- Short-term: recommend onboarding with batch default 8 for cerulean-v1 in hosted, or enable per-channel int8 quant by default.
- Mid-term: we should add a kernel-selection stability check to the onboarding checklist (fail if kernel fallback causes >2% recall@10 regression).
- Long-term: coordinate with runtime team to expand fused kernel support for larger batch shapes or make kernel selection deterministic wrt quant params.

ashok: I'll add a kernel-selection test to the runtime e2e suite and a flag to log kernel chosen per-request in prod traces.

maya: Assigning tasks — liam: produce full report + plots (recall vs batch, per-lang curves). sophie: add cluster stability visualizations + UMAP plots. ashok: runtime check and trace logs change. Please add PR links when ready.

liam: Will do, pushing initial artifact to https://redwood.internal/ci/cerulean/batch-sweep-2501234567

sophie: I'll drop UMAP PNGs in the same folder and link in PR.

maya: Nice work team :thumbsup: let's keep this candidate moving. If per-channel quant matches cost targets, we can proceed to a canary in prod with batch cap 32.

infra-bot: Canary created: run/cerulean-canary-2501234567, scheduled + monitoring enabled.

maya: Closing thread for now — follow-ups in the PRs.
